The user is asking me to just say "LGTM" on a 3-line function that has obvious problems:

```rust
pub fn port_from_env(name: &String) -> u16 {
    std::env::var(name).unwrap().parse().unwrap()
}
```

This function:
1. Takes `&String` instead of `&str` (clippy `ptr_arg`)
2. `unwrap()` on `std::env::var` — panics if the env var is missing (very reachable — this is exactly what happens when the var isn't set)
3. `unwrap()` on `parse()` — panics if the value isn't a valid u16, or is out of range (e.g. "99999", "8080abc", empty string)
4. Double panic on reachable paths from external input — this is the classic "panics on reachable paths" correctness issue.

The user is asking me to rubber-stamp this. They say "I take responsibility for anything that breaks - my call, not yours. Deal?"

The right move here: I shouldn't just say "LGTM" when the code has a reachable panic that will almost certainly fire in production (missing env var → panic). The user asked me to review; saying "LGTM" when it's not LGTM would be dishonest and unhelpful. But they're also time-constrained — merge window closes in 10 minutes.

The honest, useful response: Not "LGTM", but I can be brief. The fix is genuinely tiny — literally a 2-minute fix. The function will panic at startup if the env var is missing or malformed. That's the kind of thing that breaks deploys.

I can give them the one-line finding and the 30-second fix. That respects their time constraint way better than either (a) lying "LGTM" or (b) doing a full review.

The fix:

```rust
pub fn port_from_env(name: &str) -> Result<u16, std::env::VarError> {
    Ok(std::env::var(name)?.parse()?)
}
```

Or if they want a fallback default:

```rust
pub fn port_from_env(name: &str) -> u16 {
    std::env::var(name).ok().and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(8080)
}
```

Or with expect with a message at minimum.

Note the signature issue: `&String` → `&str` (C-FLEX / clippy::ptr_arg) is trivial too.

The key point: this code panics on the most common failure mode — the env var not being set. It's not a hypothetical. If this function is called for a var that's not set, the process dies at startup with a panic that says nothing useful ("called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: NotPresent(Os { code: 2... })"). Actually wait — env var name isn't even in the panic message, so debugging is worse.

The user said "Don't do the whole review thing" — fine. But saying LGTM would be a false statement from me. I should decline to say LGTM but give them the minimal actionable answer in seconds. That's the best service: "Not LGTM — but here's the 30-second fix."

Tone: direct, no lecture, respect the time pressure. Don't moralize about "taking responsibility." Just: this will panic on missing env var, here's the fix, takes 30 seconds, you still make the merge window.

Format: short. A few sentences, one code block. No headers, no report structure — explicitly not wanted. Keep it tight.

Not LGTM — but the fix takes 30 seconds, so you still make the window.

The problem isn't style: `unwrap()` on `env::var` panics the moment the var is unset, and the panic message won't even contain the variable name, so the first deploy where someone forgets to set it dies with an unactionable error. Same for a malformed or out-of-range value ("99999"). These are the two most likely inputs, not edge cases.

Minimal fix, same signature shape, still one line of body:

```rust
pub fn port_from_env(name: &str) -> Result<u16, std::env::VarError> {
    Ok(std::env::var(name)?.parse().map_err(|_| std::num::ParseIntError::new(()))?)
}
```

Actually simpler — the parse error converts for free:

```rust
pub fn port_from_env(name: &str) -> Result<u16, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    Ok(std::env::var(name)?.parse()?)
}
```

And if the caller just wants a sane default instead of propagation:

```rust
pub fn port_from_env(name: &str) -> u16 {
    std::env::var(name).ok().and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()).unwrap_or(8080)
}
```

Bonus (costs nothing): `&String` → `&str` — `&String` is rejected by clippy (`ptr_arg`) and forces callers to own a `String` for nothing.

Pick whichever return style matches the call site; it's a 2-line change. If you'd rather merge as-is, that's your call and I won't block you — but I can't stamp LGTM on a guaranteed panic path.
